title: LightmapGI generating light artifacts along edges of meshes
body: ### Tested versions - Reproducible on Godot v4.4.1.stable - Not reproducible on Godot v4.3.stable ### System information Windows 11 - Godot v4.4.1.stable - Compatibility, Mobile, Forward+, dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 ### Issue description When baking lightmaps with the LightmapGI node, strange light artifacts appear around the edges of meshes. These light artifacts are part of the generated lightmap. I have tried numerous possible fixes and solutions, to no avail. Possible fixes I tried: - Tweaking lightmap bias - Changing number of bounces (changing to 0 removed the artifacts) - Tweaking denoiser settings - Turning off the denoiser - Changing the compression mode on the generated .exr texture - Using a custom UV2 layout with custom padding following directions per the official documentation - Making the walls on thicker on the level I believe that this is not light leaking. In the image above, there is only one light in the scene. Also in the image above, I have used a custom .glb model exported from Blender 4.0.2. The text below is what is printed in the console when baking on Compatibility mode, although this issue is present on all rendering devices. ``` ERROR: drivers/gles3/storage/texture_storage.cpp:1792 - Parameter "texture" is null. Done baking lightmaps in 00:00:01. ``` ### Steps to reproduce 1) Create a custom .glb model, and drop it into a scene (creating a new inherited scene also works) 2) Add OmniLight3D configured to be ready for lightmap baking 3) Add LightmapGI with default settings 4) Bake the LightmapGI ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [project.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/21782120/project.zip) This MRP comes with the .glb used in the screenshot above, as well as a custom brick texture and its normal map. A basic player controller is provided to walk around the scene in-game.
